body: The capability statement's reach is edited by hand: the page and the README state what the run used and what it did not reach, and where each unreached part is proven (handler coverage, a fixture state, exploration, a component alone, the seed, the bundled fonts).
The run must use the UI graph verb; its answer goes to the model provider as the founder ratified, and the verdict fails if graph is used 0 times.
The run must use the actions verb; its answer, fields and causes, goes to the model provider as ratified, and the verdict fails if actions is used 0 times.
The run must use the lint, one screenshot and a part read; the lint's findings and the screenshot's pixels are carried to the provider, and each at 0 fails the verdict.
The run must open a select's list at least once; a list opening at 0 fails the verdict.

The run reads driver refusals by cause, the covered refusal included with its added clause on an option of a closed select and under an open list; refused_by_cause is stated as read in the report, since that clause can move wrong_calls.

The carriage to the provider is the stand's screens as the snapshot gives them: ids, names, values, snapshot texts, parts and diffs; a password value stays masked and never revealed in what the agent reads.
The seventh app, the order page, must be met, and its authored error text reaches the agent through caused, with caused_by_kind at least 1 each for panic, error and log.
Readiness drives the seven apps through the session's MCP server locally with no model, each answering the calls its goal needs, before the one firing.

The verdict counts calls and wrong calls against the 5 % bar; on a pass the page states the fifteen tools, the seven apps, the counts and the bar, on a fail the same counts, the reasons and the heading that the run failed against the bar.

The run's evidence keeps no content: the verdict holds counts, booleans and closed words only; the transcript, the check output, the server log and the kept checks are never printed, copied or committed, and whatever is committed is host-path-masked.
Exactly one firing against the provider, with no rehearsal and no retry; a run that fails or ends early is reported, and a second run waits on the founder's new word.
The stand reads no lint finding at boot as the run's starting condition, the stand apps themselves left unchanged.
Handler coverage's answer is where unreached controls are stated proven in the reach statement, beside the run's own counts.
The layout verb must be used by the run; layout answers are carried to the provider and layout at 0 fails the verdict.
Keyboard key contracts of the range input, the Cells grid, the CRUD list and the select lists' key handling: the chunk changes no control's key behaviour, only fires the agent run over them.
ARIA property reads, role mapping and the accessibility tree's state mapping rules: the chunk changes no engine or tree code.
Text contrast thresholds, the contrast ratio helper and contrast exemptions, scrollbar, hidpi, zoom and scheme rules: no visual design value changes.
The AccessKit platform adapter, its creation order and the accessibility feature's default and gating: no binary's features or adapter change.
Hidden and inert content exclusion, focusability, focus fixup and Tab order rules: the chunk touches no focus or hit-testing behaviour.
Cognitive accessibility rows (invalid state not by colour or class alone, the shared tab order table): no stand app or its states change.
The Dioxus document's render buffer, listeners from the vdom walk and the UI graph state registration hooks: no app or engine code is written.

Exactly one live run, never in CI, on the operator's login with no API key or CI secret; the client bounded by --max-budget-usd 3, the pinned model and the client timeout; no rehearsal and no retry — a second run waits on the founder's word.

The client timeout bound: whether 600 s holds 80 to 100 calls, read against the 0.2.0 run's duration; a timeout reads client-exit and spends the one run, so any change lands before the firing with its offline contract test.
The cold-agent session isolated to the escher MCP server and its session outside the root; the run reads not-isolated otherwise.
The cold-agent stand tasks: seven apps given to the agent with goals naming no element ids or app slugs, the agent's check judged by replay.
